title: Fertilisation in mammals
caption: A capacitated sperm reaches the zona pellucida; the acrosome reaction releases enzymes that digest a path through it; the sperm and egg membranes fuse and the sperm nucleus enters; the cortical reaction hardens the zona so that no further sperm can enter (preventing polyspermy); the egg completes meiosis II and the two haploid nuclei combine. In humans 23 + 23 = 46 chromosomes.
alt: Five small pictures of an egg inside its zona pellucida: a sperm at the zona; the acrosome reaction opening a gap in the zona; the sperm fused with the egg and its nucleus inside; the cortical granules releasing enzymes while a second sperm is blocked outside; and the two nuclei, 23 chromosomes each, combining.
description: Capacitated sperm reach the egg's zona pellucida.
The acrosome reaction releases enzymes that digest the zona pellucida.
The sperm membrane fuses with the egg membrane and the sperm nucleus enters.
The cortical reaction hardens the zona pellucida, so that no more sperm bind or enter: polyspermy is prevented.
The egg completes meiosis II and the two haploid nuclei combine: 23 + 23 = 46 chromosomes in humans.
Schematic: the sizes are not to scale.
